title: Empire of AI
subtitle: Dreams and Nightmares in Sam Altman's OpenAI
pitch: An investigative reporter argues OpenAI became an empire: taking data, labour and resources from around the world in the name of AGI.

chapters.g: The founding story of OpenAI and the belief that a few people should build AGI for everyone.
How the mission to benefit humanity shaped, and justified, OpenAI's choices.
Inside the company as it grows and its culture forms.
The bet on scale: bigger models, more data, more compute.
How the scaling strategy pushed costs and ambitions ever higher.
OpenAI's rise to the centre of the AI world.
How commercial pressure affected research openness.
The turn toward products and revenue.
The workers, often in poorer countries, who label data and filter disturbing content.
Inside the split between safety focused staff and those pushing to ship.
ChatGPT's launch and the height of OpenAI's influence.
The water, power and land costs of data centres, including in Latin America.
The rival visions of AI's promise and peril inside the company.
The lead up to the November 2023 crisis.
The board's attempt to remove Sam Altman.
The behind the scenes fight during and after the firing.
Altman's return and what it meant for OpenAI's governance and safety.
Hao's argument that the AI industry follows the pattern of old empires.
What a different, more accountable path for AI could look like.

ideas: The AI industry concentrates power like an empire.
AI's costs fall on workers and communities far from Silicon Valley.
Mission language can justify almost anything.
Governance at OpenAI failed under pressure.

args.a: The pursuit of AGI by a few companies is extractive and dangerous.
args.c: Some readers think the book is too one sided, and safety researchers note it pays less attention to catastrophic risk from AI itself.

questions: Is 'empire' a fair word for today's AI companies?
Who pays the hidden costs of AI where you live?

quiz.q: What is Hao's main metaphor for the AI industry?
quiz.w: She argues the industry extracts resources like an empire.

quiz.q: Which event is covered in 'The Gambit'?
o: The board's attempt to remove Sam Altman
